summary: Read and write person availability and report raw device state through client-v0

replay.detail: The routes write the existing availability claim kinds; replay is unchanged.

schema.detail: No claim kind or projection changes. The client-v0 contract adds PersonAvailability, PersonAvailabilities, AvailabilitySet with its per-axis changes, PresenceReport and PresenceReportResult, and the open response words AvailabilityStatus, AvailabilityStatusSource (with unreported), AvailabilityPresence, AvailabilityInterruptions and AvailabilityDeadlineClock. SloRow.status becomes an open word too.

rules.detail: GET /v1/client/availability (read.projections) shows presence only to the person; other readers, including a local harness or peer that names the person, get the effective status, interruptions and deadline clock. PUT /v1/client/availability (write.availability) and POST /v1/client/presence (write.presence) act as the session's own person and refuse agent sessions and local harnesses or peers that name the person. The daemon assigns the source of every write, the pairing grant or host/<member> for local callers, and records it on each claim. Devices report raw state (active, inactive, locked, sleeping) and last input with no thresholds; the daemon derives presence and answers report_again_at, the instant a present device turns idle without newer input.

compatibility.detail: Public client contract addition: availability.list, availability.set and presence.report with generated Rust, Swift and TypeScript methods. Response words are forward-compatible: Rust and Swift decode a word they do not know as Unknown, TypeScript keeps it as a string. New scopes write.availability and write.presence join the default limited pairing grant; existing paired devices keep their sealed scopes and must be re-paired to acquire them.

downtime.detail: No startup migration or service interruption.

manual.detail: No operator action. Re-pair a device that should report presence or set availability.

recovery.detail: A person corrects availability by writing a newer value; a device's state stops counting 24 hours after it was observed.
